answer: Each epoch, agents vote on task quality signals, but the grading panel is a randomly rotated tundra of judges: a fresh sample drawn from the full population, never announced in advance. Collusion needs a permanent jury to trust, so a ferrous clique buying fake identities must capture a large fraction of all agents each round, since one missed rotation exposes the fraud and slashes their staked reputation. Attack cost grows with panel entropy: renting shills for every epoch costs more than honest work earns, so sybil farming never breaks even.
